petratouromiou.name: Aphrodite's Rock
petratouromiou.slogan: The sea stack where the goddess of love stepped ashore.
petratouromiou.line: There the moist breath of the western wind wafted her over the waves of the loud-moaning sea in soft foam.
petratouromiou.by: Homeric Hymn 6 to Aphrodite, trans. Evelyn-White, 1914

paphosmosaics.name: Paphos Mosaics
paphosmosaics.slogan: Gods and hunters in stone, still bright after 1,700 years.
paphosmosaics.line: The House of Dionysos dates to the 3rd century AD, and the wider Paphos site became a World Heritage Site in 1980.

kourion.name: Kourion Theatre
kourion.slogan: A Roman stage on a cliff, with Episkopi Bay as the backdrop.
kourion.line: Built in the late 2nd century BCE and enlarged under Trajan, the theatre once seated up to 3,500 people.

sthilarion.name: St Hilarion Castle
sthilarion.slogan: Towers on a ridge, with the whole north coast below.
sthilarion.line: It is the best preserved ruin of the three former strongholds in the Kyrenia mountains.

selimiye.name: Selimiye Mosque
selimiye.slogan: A French Gothic cathedral with two minarets, in the heart of Nicosia.
selimiye.line: Built as the Cathedral of St Sophia and consecrated in 1326, it saw Lusignan kings crowned before the Ottomans added minarets in 1570.
